A map of the code.

This is a working learning project. Follow one action from the browser to the database before reading every file.

1. Start with the data

apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma defines projects, assignments, comments, and activity. Projects and assignments belong to an organization.

2. Follow “Complete assignment”

  1. features/workspace/graphql/workspace.operations.ts{" "} defines the frontend mutation.
  2. modules/assignments/graphql/assignments.resolver.ts{" "} passes it to a use case.
  3. use-cases/change-assignment-status.ts checks access and performs the transaction.
  4. policies/assignment.policy.ts checks the actor;{" "} domain/assignment.rules.ts checks the state.
  5. Prisma saves the assignment and an activity entry together.
  6. platform/redis/pubsub.service.ts invalidates the cache and publishes after commit.
  7. The subscription notifies other tabs;{" "} hooks/use-workspace.ts refreshes their data.

3. Compare a query

queries/list-assignments.ts filters by organization before returning rows. assignment-fields.resolver.ts computes capabilities only when requested. The dashboard query caches aggregates in real Redis for 30 seconds.

4. Try the permission boundaries

Maya can manage team assignments. Alice and Bob can change their own work. Leo can only read. Eva is in another organization. These demo identities are deliberately spoofable: replace them with verified sessions before production.

5. Know the limits

Redis notifications are transient, not a durable queue. Clients refresh on reconnect and focus. Sentry is optional and disabled until a DSN is configured. The original orders lab still uses its small in-memory store; Fieldwork uses PostgreSQL.

The full guide is in docs/START-HERE.md. Setup and test commands are in README.md.
